claims.text: The initial alloy contains approximately 40 at% Ti, 40 at% Ni, 10 at% Cr, and 8 at% Al.
The initial Ti-Ni-Cr-Al alloy is a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The intervention incorporates 2 at% Ce during casting.
Ce acts as a trace dopant in the proposed alloy.
Homogenization at 1000°C for 4 hours followed by controlled slow cooling will encourage Ce segregation to grain boundaries.
Adding Ce will produce localized Ce segregation at grain boundaries.
Ce segregation will stabilize grain-boundary interfaces and enhance grain-boundary cohesion.
Segregated Ce will reduce grain-boundary mobility and impede grain-boundary sliding.
Reduced grain-boundary mobility caused by Ce will impede diffusional creep at elevated temperature.
The Ce-doped alloy will have greater creep resistance than the undoped alloy at elevated temperature.
The Ce-doped alloy will maintain or enhance elevated-temperature ductility relative to the undoped alloy.
The predicted benefit depends on avoiding detrimental brittle intermetallic phases.
The intervention is applicable to alloys containing around 40 at% Ti and 40 at% Ni.
Performance improvement is expected under high-temperature conditions above approximately 800°C.

contradictions.description: The proposed alloy has approximately 40 at% Ti and 40 at% Ni, while the boundary requires every element to remain within 5–35 at%; both primary constituents exceed the stated maximum.

The undoped alloy contains only four stated elements, and the Ce-modified alloy adds Ce at only 2 at%. Thus neither composition satisfies the stated definition of at least five elements present at 5–35 at% each, despite the claim that the intervention remains within that definition.
